verdict.rationale: Motion's own docs say it blocks calendar time for recurring tasks (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly) and reshuffles the whole day or week when meetings run long or emergencies arise, so recurring blocks are re-placed rather than dropped. Meeting windows such as 'focused mornings' and daily meeting caps help protect focus periods. However, no dedicated focus-time or habit-defense feature is documented, and nothing explicitly says recurring items are kept rather than dropped when conflicts appear. Missing for 10: an explicit focus-time/habit defense feature, documentation that recurring blocks are guaranteed to be preserved and moved on conflict, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a knowledge worker, the product auto-defends recurring focus time and habits, flexibly moving them when conflicts appear instead of dropping them

citations.quote: Create daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly tasks and Motion's AI Task Manager will block time on your calendar regularly
When meetings run long or emergencies arise, Motion reshuffles your entire day (and week) in seconds—protecting your time and mental bandwidth from manual reorganization.
Set your ideal meeting windows. Whether you prefer focused mornings, back-to-back afternoons, or meeting-free Fridays
Set daily limits and watch Motion enforce them automatically. When you hit your threshold, your calendar becomes unbookable
